title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Pipeline Run. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pipeline Run
options.lineage: CI/CD pipeline views: stages, jobs, statuses, job logs
options.thesis: Your career is shown as one pipeline run: each employer a stage, each shipped thing a passed job, and contacting you is the manual job at the end.
materials: one deep green field owning the opening
options.viewport: Full-bleed green field: your name and 'Lead Full Stack Developer' set huge, and under it the pipeline graph running left to right (WeHELP, ARK-X, Piyes, Now) with job pills ticking to passed. The orange 'Run: contact' manual job sits at the end of the graph.
options.risk: Can read as dev-tool cosplay to a non-technical recruiter if the headline is not plain language.

raised.raise: Shipped work is drawn solid; in-progress work (AWS prep, Telegram bot in testing) is drawn dashed. Honest scale becomes a visual rule.
One loud colour is reserved for the action only: the orange manual job that contacts you or gets the CV.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: a very large name against small mono job labels, no decoration.
State accumulates: jobs a visitor opens stay marked as read, so the graph records their path.

options.label: The README
options.lineage: engineering documentation sites and well-kept READMEs
options.thesis: The portfolio as the docs page of a well-run project: sticky table of contents, plain sections, tables of facts.
options.viewport: Left rail with section links, right column opening with name, role, three proof lines and Contact / CV buttons.
options.risk: Also where most developer portfolios in this style land; clear but not memorable.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Your name as one giant letterform that visitors reshape with sliders.
options.viewport: A giant 'A' with weight and width sliders, facts in tiny mono labels.
options.risk: The toy is about type, not about what you built.
options.case: Hiring leads do not identify with a foundry tool, and the sliders carry no career fact.

options.label: Pattern Envelope
options.lineage: home sewing pattern envelopes and tissue
options.thesis: Projects as numbered pattern pieces laid on a cutting layout.
options.viewport: Envelope front with three lettered views of the work.
options.risk: A craft metaphor a CTO has to decode.
options.case: Loses on both audience identification and clarity.

options.label: Paste-up Zine
options.thesis: The career as a xeroxed flyer with ransom-note headlines.
options.risk: Legibility and trust drop for a hiring audience.
options.case: Grit works against the reliability you need to prove.
options.kept: One day-glo colour reserved for the action.

options.label: Magazine Quiz
options.thesis: A quiz that tallies answers into a verdict about hiring you.
options.viewport: Lettered checkbox rows over torn photos.
options.risk: Tone is wrong for lead roles.
options.case: Makes the visitor work before any proof appears.
options.kept: State that accumulates as the visitor moves.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Skills as a row of needles behind glass.
options.risk: Needle levels would be invented skill scores.
options.case: Skill levels are not facts in the knowledge base, so the form forces a false claim.
options.kept: Identical units repeated as a ruler.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.thesis: One amber hall with a half sun at the far wall.
options.viewport: Amber duotone horizon, name low on the line.
options.risk: Atmosphere with no room for proof.
options.case: Mood over evidence; fails the one-minute decision.
options.kept: One colour owning the whole room.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio everyone ships: dark hero, name, photo, project cards, skills grid, contact form.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role left, portrait right, two buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other candidates by design.
